anthropic.summary: Official Anthropic cloud API setup for D3m0n. No Anthropic account, key, live request, or paid inference is configured or tested in this workspace; Ollama remains the fresh-chat default.
steps: Open D3m0n AI settings and select Anthropic.
Use the official HTTPS base URL https://api.anthropic.com; do not use an arbitrary proxy for a cloud key.

Create or obtain an Anthropic API key in Claude Console, enter it through the masked replacement-only field, and save it; use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only as an environment fallback when intentionally configured.
Discover available models through Anthropic GET /v1/models or enter an account-approved current model ID; do not hardcode a stale catalogue.
Run the dashboard metadata/readiness Test, understanding that it is not a paid inference test, then make Anthropic the default only if desired; the change applies to new chats.

claude-code.summary: Anthropic's online terminal coding agent. It requires an Anthropic subscription, Console/API account, or supported enterprise/cloud configuration; it is separate from the locally installed Ollama provider and is not an offline model.
steps: Confirm a supported environment (Windows 10 1809+/Server 2019+, Ubuntu 20.04+, macOS 13+, Debian 10+, or Alpine 3.19+), 4 GB+ RAM, x64/ARM64, an internet connection, and a project directory.

Install in the project environment: Linux/WSL/macOS uses `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`; native Windows PowerShell uses `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex`; WinGet uses `winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode`. Git for Windows is optional but recommended for native Windows Bash support.
Open a new terminal and run `claude --version`; use `claude doctor` for read-only installation/settings diagnostics.

Start `claude` in the project directory and complete browser login with Claude Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise or use a Claude Console/API or supported enterprise/cloud setup. `claude auth login --console` selects Console/API billing. Never put credentials in dashboard code, URLs, logs, or browser storage.

Use `claude auth status` for redacted authentication status, `claude auth logout` to log out, and `/login` inside a session to re-authenticate. An approved `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` changes credential precedence and may change billing.

For a cautious first session, retain manual permissions or use plan mode; review commands and edits. `claude -p` runs a one-off query, `claude -c` continues the latest conversation, and `claude -r` resumes one.

For dashboard readiness, report CLI presence/version and redacted auth/diagnostic status separately. Do not infer model readiness from CLI presence or authentication, and do not run paid inference, alter phones, download models, or expose keys in a metadata test.
Treat the existing d3m0n-ollama.service/qwen3.5:4b loopback Ollama setup as a separate on-device provider; no Claude Code installation, login, account, or credentials are assumed by this guide.

ollama.summary: Use the existing Ubuntu user service d3m0n-ollama.service at loopback http://127.0.0.1:11434 with the installed qwen3.5:4b model. Cloud access is disabled and no API key is required for local requests.
steps: Set the provider base URL to http://127.0.0.1:11434 and keep the provider local-only.
Set the default model to the exact installed tag qwen3.5:4b; do not guess additional model names.
Leave the API-key field empty because the local Ollama API does not require authentication.
Use metadata/readiness checks only with authorization: discover installed models via GET /api/tags and loaded models via GET /api/ps; do not infer readiness from a cloud request.
If the service is unavailable, have the service owner manage the existing d3m0n-ollama.service; do not reinstall, expose the port, pull models, or enable cloud access as part of dashboard setup.

on-device.summary: This provider runs inside the upstream Android ghost-app through Chaquopy and its Kotlin OnDeviceLLM runtime. It is not a second Ollama server and is unavailable in this Ubuntu-hosted Python process.
steps: Use Ollama / qwen3.5:4b for the current wireless-ADB fleet; it is the installed and verified local option.
For true phone-resident inference, build/install the compatible upstream ghost-app with the com.ghostinthedroid.app.ondevice.OnDeviceLLM runtime and a supported registered model.
Run the agent inside that Android app so the java/Chaquopy bridge exists. Merely installing a model on this Ubuntu PC does not enable this provider.
Android 9, device ABI, model licensing, storage and runtime compatibility must be confirmed separately. Test readiness here reports the bridge is missing; no automatic phone install is performed.

openrouter.summary: Hosted OpenAI-compatible model gateway; not installed or configured here. Setup requires a user-owned account, bounded API key, official HTTPS base URL, and current model slug.
steps: Create an OpenRouter account and API key at https://openrouter.ai/keys; set a credit limit and keep the key private.
Select OpenRouter in D3m0n AI settings and use https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 as the official base URL.
Enter the key only in the masked replacement field and save; use the explicit clear control to remove it. Never expose it in URLs, logs, browser storage, bundles, or errors.
Discover or select a current model slug from GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models; do not assume a fixed catalog.
Save the provider and optionally make it the default for new chats; existing active chats remain unchanged.
Use Test only as metadata/readiness validation: it must not perform paid inference, and success does not prove model inference or credits.

vllm.summary: Configure vLLM only when an operator has separately provisioned a compatible host, model, and private OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint. vLLM is not installed or verified in this workspace; existing Ollama is a separate provider.
steps: Check the official vLLM hardware and installation matrix for the intended Linux or supported accelerator host; do not install on an occupied GPU.

Create an isolated Python environment and install the hardware-specific vLLM build following the version-matched official instructions; the stable quickstart example uses Python 3.12 and uv for NVIDIA.
Choose a supported model and start it with `vllm serve <exact-model-id>`; model downloads and host provisioning are operator actions outside this guide.
Expose the documented OpenAI-compatible API, normally at port 8000, and optionally configure `--api-key` or `VLLM_API_KEY` with network controls; the key does not protect every endpoint.
In D3m0n, enter the operator-supplied private base URL ending in `/v1`, the exact served model ID, and a key only if the server requires one; do not use the Ollama URL.
Use the dashboard metadata/readiness test or an approved private client to check `/v1/models` and chat compatibility; no live request or model download was performed for this guide.
